title: Inseparable Phrasal Verbs: Look After
grammarTitle: Inseparable Phrasal Verbs — The Object Always After
grammarNote: Неразделяемые фразовые глаголы (inseparable phrasal verbs) нельзя разделить объектом. Объект — существительное или местоимение — всегда стоит ПОСЛЕ всего фразового глагола (verb + particle). В отличие от разделяемых глаголов, с неразделяемыми НЕЛЬЗЯ поставить объект между глаголом и частицей.

grammarTable.subject: look after
grammarTable.example: "Look AFTER your health." / "Look after IT." (never: ✗"look your health after")

grammarTable.subject: run into
grammarTable.example: "I ran INTO an old friend." / "I ran into HIM." (never: ✗"ran him into")

grammarTable.subject: come across
grammarTable.example: "She came ACROSS a great book." / "came across IT."

grammarTable.subject: get on with

grammarTable.subject: deal with
grammarTable.example: "She deals WITH the problem." / "deals with IT."

grammarTable.subject: go through
grammarTable.example: "I've gone THROUGH a lot." / "going through IT."

rows.example: "Look after the children." / "Look after them." (care for)
"I ran into Rustam in the library." / "ran into him." (meet by chance)
"She came across a useful article." (find by chance)
"He gets on well with his supervisor." (have a good relationship)
"She's dealing with a difficult situation." (handle/manage)
"She's been going through a tough time." (experience)
"The professor looked into the complaint." (investigate)
"I'm looking forward to the holidays." (be excited about)
"WKU stands for 'West Kazakhstan University'." (represent/mean)
"She takes after her mother." (resemble/be like)
"I can't keep up with the pace." (maintain the same speed/level)
"She puts up with a lot." (tolerate)
"I'm looking forward to meeting you." (not: ✗ "looking you forward to meeting")
"She's trying to catch up with the class." (reach the same level)
"Get on with your work!" (continue) OR "I get on well with her." (relationship)
"I can't put up with the noise." (tolerate)
"She's cutting down on sugar." (reduce)
"The film didn't live up to my expectations." (meet expectations)
"Turn it off." ✅ / "Turn off it." ✗ → pronoun INSIDE
"Look after it." ✅ / ✗ "Look it after." → object ALWAYS AFTER
Check a dictionary! Or test: ✗ "look it after" sounds wrong → inseparable.
"Call off" = inseparable (cancel). "Pick up" = separable. You must learn which is which.

grammarExtra.title: ❌ Common errors with inseparable phrasal verbs

rows.example: "Look after IT" is actually CORRECT! Objects go AFTER the phrasal verb. "Look after it." ✅
✅ "Look AFTER it." — object AFTER "after", not between "look" and "after".
✅ "I ran into him." — object AFTER the particle "into".
✅ "She looks forward TO it." — object after the whole phrasal verb.

grammarTip:
Неразделяемые фразовые глаголы — объект ВСЕГДА после:

"Look after the children." ✅
"Look after them." ✅
✗ "Look them after." — НИКОГДА!

"I ran into an old friend." ✅
"I ran into him." ✅
✗ "I ran him into." — НИКОГДА!

💡 Как отличить разделяемые от неразделяемых?
1) Проверь: *"ran him into"* — звучит неправильно?
   → Скорее всего неразделяемый!
2) Используй словарь — хорошие словари помечают Sep. (separable)
   и Insep. (inseparable).

⚠️ Трёхкомпонентные фразовые глаголы (look forward to,
put up with, keep up with) — ВСЕГДА неразделяемые!

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form of the inseparable phrasal verb.
exercises.hint: "Look after" is inseparable. Object goes AFTER the whole phrasal verb: "looks after HER HEALTH." ✅

exercises.text: Choose the correct sentence with "run into".
exercises.hint: "run into" = inseparable. Object goes AFTER: "ran into HIM." ✅ (NOT "ran him into")
"get on with" = inseparable 3-part phrasal verb. "She gets on well WITH her colleagues." ✅

exercises.text: "She came the book across" is a correct inseparable phrasal verb.
exercises.hint: ✅ "She came ACROSS the book." — object always AFTER the full inseparable phrasal verb.
"deal with" = inseparable. "She dealt WITH the problem." ✅
"put up with" = 3-part inseparable phrasal verb. "I can't PUT UP WITH the noise." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct sentence with "look forward to".
exercises.hint: "look forward to" = 3-part inseparable. "I'm looking forward TO IT." ✅ (always after)

exercises.text: "Look after him" — test: "Look him after" sounds ___.
exercises.hint: ✗ "Look him after" — sounds wrong → inseparable. ✅ "Look AFTER him."

exercises.text: "She's cutting down ___ coffee because she's too stressed."
exercises.hint: "cut down on" = inseparable. "She's cutting down ON coffee." ✅

exercises.text: "I went through it last night." — Is this correct?
opts: No — it should be "went it through"
Yes — "go through" is inseparable, object after
No — it should be "went through last night"
No — it is wrong; use "it went through me"
exercises.correct: Yes — "go through" is inseparable, object after
exercises.hint: "go through" = inseparable. "I went THROUGH it." ✅ Object (it) comes after the whole phrasal verb.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form with "stand for".
exercises.hint: "stand for" = inseparable. "WKU stands FOR 'West Kazakhstan University'." ✅ The object goes after "for".

exercises.text: "She takes her mother after." — Correct or incorrect?
opts: Incorrect — should be "takes after her mother"
Incorrect — should be "takes it after her mother"
exercises.correct: Incorrect — should be "takes after her mother"
exercises.hint: "take after" = inseparable. ✅ "She TAKES AFTER her mother." Object always after the particle.

questions.text: "Look after" is inseparable. Which is correct?
questions.hint: Inseparable → object ALWAYS after the full phrasal verb. "Look AFTER it." ✅

questions.text: "I ran into him." — This is correct because:
opts: "into" is a preposition, not a particle
"run into" is inseparable — object goes after
questions.correct: "run into" is inseparable — object goes after

questions.text: "She puts up with a lot." — "puts up with" is:
questions.hint: "put up with" = 3-part inseparable phrasal verb. Object always after "with". ✅

questions.text: "She came across a great book." — With pronoun: "She came ___ ."
questions.hint: Inseparable: object after. "She came ACROSS IT." ✅ (NOT "came it across")
"get on with someone" = have a good relationship. "Get on with your work!" = continue.
"look forward TO" — "to" is part of this 3-part phrasal verb. ✅
✅ "She dealt WITH it." — "deal with" is inseparable. Object goes after "with".
"go through" = to experience (a difficulty) or to examine (a document) carefully.
"keep up with" = inseparable 3-part. "I can't keep up WITH the pace." ✅

questions.text: "WKU stands for West Kazakhstan University." — "stand for" here means:
questions.hint: "stand for" = to represent or mean (an abbreviation or principle). ✅

questions.text: How do you tell if a phrasal verb is inseparable?
opts: The object cannot go between the parts
questions.correct: The object cannot go between the parts
questions.hint: Inseparable = the object cannot be placed between the verb and particle(s). Test by trying to split: sounds wrong → inseparable.
"go through" = to experience. "She's been going THROUGH a lot lately." ✅

opts: She takes care of her mother
questions.hint: "take after someone" = to resemble or be similar to (usually a family member).
"look into something" = to investigate or examine more carefully.
"come across" = inseparable. Object after: "She came ACROSS IT accidentally." ✅

questions.text: What is the main rule for inseparable phrasal verbs?
opts: Object goes between verb and particle
Object always goes after the complete phrasal verb
questions.correct: Object always goes after the complete phrasal verb
questions.hint: Inseparable = object ALWAYS after. "Look after it." / "Run into him." — never split. ✅
